This is a complicated subject where proponents only show one side of the story. I know some of the facts in the graphic are correct. Let's assume all the facts are correct. That doesn't change the fact that a higher minimum wage might be a bad idea.

Most of the people supporting a higher minimum wage have not lived long enough to see what increased expenses does to a company. When expenses increase, the first people to lose their jobs are the low wage-earners. Raising the minimum wage will cut jobs in those areas like: fast food, restaurants, production lines, and retail. But why?

  • Executive bonuses are contractual and must be paid if the exec achieves certain metrics. Thus, the company must have that money in the bank if and when the execs achieve their metrics.
  • Megaprofit Fortune 500 companies can afford the increase...in some cases. But many businesses are franchises owned by small businessmen. 99% of businesses in the US are small businesses under 500 employees and small business is the biggest employer in the US (http://www.sba.gov). Those businesses will have to cut jobs if the min wage is raised because their sales don't automatically increase if their expenses increase. Out of the people asking for min wage increases, most are not old enough to know that in McDonalds in the 1980s we had 8-9 people working a store in a typical summer day (winters are slower). Now they have 3-4 people working there. Automation has not increased significantly during this time as I worked there in the 1980s and my wife worked there recently.
  • Franchisees will also have to raise the prices of their products to cover increased expenses. This means fewer people coming in to buy their product. Fast food has such low nutritional value these days, and is more expensive than getting a bag of frozen Chinese food which actually has real vegetables, that a bag of frozen food for 2 people is less than a meal at a fast food restaurant. So I just don't go out to fast food anymore.
  • The people who manage to keep their job and get a min wage raise will spend more but this will not add significantly to individual businesses because the gain will be spread extremely thinly. But most will not get out of poverty or the debt cycle because of the poor choices they make. Their highest priorities, by my actual observation of living with the poor for 40+ years, is: booze, cigarettes, high speed internet, smart phones, motorcycles, boats, and other luxuries they cannot afford. Giving them more money does not change the poor decisions they make whether it's via a higher minimum wage or a fixed amount every month (in lieu of welfare programs.)
  • Shareholders are the next in line to get paid and the company will reduce employees, and hire employees more experienced with computers and automation systems, which help increase efficiency. Most poor people and min wage earners are not known for being computer savvy.
  • Companies will further reduce employment because employees are the biggest expense, ask any accountant. (I have 4 years of accounting in my past.) Employers will reduce employment in order to increase dividends. So the low-wage employees further suffer from any increase in corporate expense.
  • In order to reduce expenses, and keep the company alive, more production labor will simply be shipped overseas.

Yes, the economy has gotten worse over the years. Yes the min wage has not kept place with inflation for 20+ years, but there are reasons for that, some of which I explained above. Plus the increase in out-of-pocket medical expenses, and college tuition. Obamacare taxes on companies and people, means there are fewer min wage jobs out there, and also a min wage earner has less for other basic living expenses.

The problem is a little more complicated than "the min wage has not kept pace with expenses". And the solution is more complicated also.

Let me play devil's advocate here.

There are three outcomes in the event of a nuclear blast. One, you get killed quickly, anything from vaporized to a lethal dose of radiation. Two, the bomb blast is sufficiently far away that you are not affected by it at all. Three, something between outcome one and two. For the first two options, hiding under the desk is pointless, but probably won't affect whether you survive or not. For the third option, there is always the possibility that a nuclear blast will shake the ground and cause damage to buildings beyond where you would be vaporized or hit with a lethal dose of radiation. In this case, hiding under the desk will provide some protection if things start falling off shelves or from the ceiling or if windows shatter. Of course, the desk probably won't save Johnny and Susie if the building collapses, but it might save them if a light fixture fell.

If the kids were to be let out from the school, there is a chance that they would be run over by a car or otherwise harmed in the ensuing general panic. Also, even if the kids could get somewhat far away from the school, without knowing exactly where an incoming bomb might detonate the kids might end up running closer to ground zero and not away from it.
